risks: Sending the context switch as its own exec -- the record measured that this silently scopes every later query to the wrong domain and produces confident wrong answers, not errors.
Parsing the object dump positionally or by line number instead of by nested key -- the format has hundreds of keys per object and their order is not a contract.

Reading the connection table through an awk pipeline on the server 'to keep the output small' -- the reduction belongs in Java so the raw text is parsed and dropped under T-7 and so no logic hides in a shell string.
Inventing the cluster_object block's inner field names instead of raising a RELAY_QUESTION if the record does not settle them.
Keeping a mgmt_cli code path 'as a fallback' -- the closed set is the measured set only.

in: Closed command set, replaced: (1) domain enumeration -- the management-server utility that lists the domain management servers (record section 4 item 1, the '$MDSVERUTIL AllCMAs' form); (2) per domain per object type, ONE shell command line that performs the domain context switch AND the query in the same shell: the 'mdsenv <DOMAIN>' context command followed on the same line by cpmiquerybin with the 'object' result type and a type filter (record section 4 item 5 form with a type filter instead of a name filter; section 10 row 4), for exactly the three object types the contract classifies -- gateway, cluster member, cluster (type values as the record's section 4 item 3 filter shows); (3) the connection-table read -- 'netstat -an' on the management server, issued twice separated by the caller's CS-3 interval, filtered and reduced IN JAVA (never by an awk pipeline on the server, so the raw output is parsed in memory and dropped, T-7). The domain identifier and every other interpolated value is quoted as one shell argument. No mgmt_cli anywhere. No script upload. No other command (record section 0).

Same-shell constraint (record section 3 row 2, section 10): the context switch and the query are one ExecSpec command string. A test asserts that no ExecSpec the adapter ever sends contains the context command without a query on the same line, and that no query is ever sent without its context. THE DECISIVE TEST -- write it first against the current adapter and observe it failing (the current adapter has no context command at all).

Parser, replaced: a parser for the cpmiquerybin 'object' tree format as the record's section 10 row 4 describes it -- each object begins with an opening parenthesis followed by its name at column 0; fields are ':key (value)' leaves or ':key (' ... ')' nested blocks; values may be quoted or empty; the stable identifier is the 'chkpf_uid' leaf inside the 'AdminInfo' block. Parse as a stream (T-7), tolerate unknown keys (hundreds exist), never rely on column position, treat a missing key as ABSENT (contract CR-0: a '?' field may be absent) and an empty value as EMPTY (one arm of HR-2, never repaired). Remove MinimalJson if nothing else uses it. Build synthetic fixture texts in that format (invented names, addresses, identifiers -- follow the existing WorkerFixtures discipline).

Field bindings, rebound at the one site (FB-2, every entry stays UNVERIFIED): STABLE_IDENTIFIER -> the AdminInfo/chkpf_uid leaf; DISPLAY_NAME -> name; PRODUCT_FLAG -> cp_products_installed; OWN_ADDRESS -> ipaddr; MANAGEMENT_ADDRESS -> mgmt_ip; CLUSTER_REFERENCE_IDENTIFIER and CLUSTER_REFERENCE_DISPLAY_NAME -> the identifier and name carried inside the cluster_object reference (record section 5 row 4: 'a stable identifier alongside the display name' -- bind to what the block carries, mark UNVERIFIED); MODEL -> appliance_type; SOFTWARE_VERSION -> svn_version_name; MANAGEMENT_PLANE_CONNECTION_STATE -> connection_state; DOMAIN_IDENTIFIER -> the domain enumeration's per-line value; CONNECTION_TABLE_ADDRESS/PORT/STATE -> the netstat foreign-address and state columns as the record's section 4 item 6 shows. Remove SESSION_IDENTIFIER (no session token exists in the measured method). VIRT_HOST_FLAG and VIRT_SYSTEM_FLAG bind to a DIFFERENT attribute per object type (record section 10, field-binding consequence): extend ManagementApiFieldBinding so an entry may be scoped to an ObjectType (forRole(role, objectType)), keep one field per (role, object type), and state in the class comment that this is the measured shape and that whether it satisfies FB-2's 'exactly one field' is noted for the contract's freeze owner -- do not amend the contract. Keep FieldBindingIsolationTest passing against the new literals.

Object type mapping: the three type filter values map to ObjectType.GATEWAY / MEMBER / CLUSTER; the object's own 'type' leaf is read only to confirm the filter, never to classify beyond the contract's three types (CL-4). The flags feed ClassificationFlags exactly as before; nothing in the domain core's rules changes.

Connection table (section 7.4, record section 4 items 6/6a and section 6): from each 'netstat -an' reading, in Java: take rows whose state is the established state or a not-yet-established state, derive the channel port as the most frequent foreign port among established rows (CS-6b) unless a configured port is supplied, reduce to one state per foreign address (CS-6a), keep only addresses that are also a candidate's management address, and apply CS-3 across the two readings (agree failing -> FAILING_TO_COMPLETE; disagree -> IN_TRANSITION; no entry in either -> ABSENT). NoNumericPortLiteralTest must keep passing.

Check 17 request count: one session + one domain enumeration + exactly one object query per domain per object type (no pagination in the object result type) ; the two connection-table reads are not counted, as the current gate document already states. Update the adapter's count and its test.
